newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economic recovery needs to be stronger - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan economic recovery needs to be stronger - BOJ.

text.p: Japan's economic recovery needs to gain strength in order to become self-sustainable, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita was quoted as saying on Tuesday.

"For our nation's economy to move on to a self-sustained recovery track, the current recovery needs to gain more strength," said Matsushita's speech to a convention of non-life insurers, which was read by deputy BOJ governor Toshihiko Fukui.
The economic recovery is spreading to a wider area, but the pace remains gradual, said the speech.
Growth in industrial production in general remained slow with some fluctuations, reflecting inventory drawdowns in the semiconductor industry and other sectors, he said.

The BOJ's quarterly "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment, released last month, showed improvement in corporate business confidence had stalled, the governor said. The declining trend in domestic prices is coming to a halt, he added.

"In managing our monetary policy for the time being, we think it is appropriate to keep putting emphasis on making the basis for an economic recovery more solid, while monitoring economic developments carefully," Matsushita said.
Japan also needs to carry out effective deregulation in order to enhance structural adjustments in the economy and draw more strength from the private sector, he said.

Matsushita said new organisations and laws to deal with bad loans have made it possible to be more efficient and quick in coping with failures of financial firms while maintaining stability in the financial system.

He said that the basis for rebuilding an efficient and stable financial system was to use market mechanisms to the full and make sure participants understand market rules and the principle of taking responsibility for their own actions.
In Matsushita's speech, he said he welcomed the decision by some financial firms to use mark-to-market accounting methods and to expand the disclosure of their bad loans.
Matsushita is attending a monthly meeting of the Bank for International Settlements in Basle, Switzerland, and is due to return today.
